network.streamIdleHelp: Max time to wait for next chunk before closing a stalled stream
network.maxConnsHelp: Max TCP connections per provider host. For HTTP/2 providers (e.g. Bedrock), each connection supports ~100 concurrent streams.
network.keepAliveHelp: Idle keep-alive for pooled connections. Set below the upstream server's keep-alive to avoid reusing connections it has already closed.
network.enforceHttp2Help: Force HTTP/2 on provider connections. Relevant for net/http-based providers (e.g. Bedrock) where each HTTP/2 connection supports ~100 concurrent streams.
network.http2PingHelp: Idle seconds before a client-initiated HTTP/2 keepalive PING. Prevents intermediaries from cutting quiet streams and long generations. 0 disables; requires Enforce HTTP/2.
network.allowPrivateHelp: Allow connections to private IPs (e.g. 10.x, 192.168.x). Required for providers on a LAN, k8s pod network, or private VPC. Cloud metadata addresses (169.254.x.x) are always blocked.
network.skipTlsHelp: Disable TLS certificate verification for provider connections. This bypasses server certificate validation and should be used only as a last resort when a trusted CA chain cannot be configured. Prefer ca_cert_pem for self-signed or private CA deployments.
network.caCertPemHelp: PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for provider endpoint connections (e.g. self-signed or internal CA).

promptCache.autoInjectHelp: Agentic clients such as Codex send no cache markers, so the cached prefix follows the newest message and every turn is billed as a cache write. Turning this on marks the first cacheable block instead, which keeps the cached region stable so turn 2 onward is a cache read. Requests that already carry their own cache markers are never modified, and models without explicit caching are left alone.
promptCache.ttlHelp: A longer TTL costs more per cache write but survives gaps between turns. Providers that cannot carry a TTL ignore this.
promptCache.injectionPointsHelp: Optional. Target specific messages instead of the first cacheable block. Adding any point <medium>replaces</medium> the default strategy rather than adding to it. Each point needs a role, an index, or both. At most four markers are injected, matching the provider ceiling.
promptCache.pointNeedsRoleOrIndex: Each point needs a role, an index, or both.

openaiForm.disableStoreHelp: With the Responses API, store defaults to true, and when it is on, the generated response is stored for later retrieval via API. keys.weightHelp: Determines traffic distribution between keys. Higher weights receive more requests. Not used when adaptive load balancing is enabled - key selection is then based on live performance.
keys.copilotTokenHelp: Requires Network Config > Base URL set to the host the token was issued for, because a Copilot token does not carry one. Also expires after about 30 minutes, and Bifrost cannot refresh a token it did not mint, so prefer the GitHub App below for anything long-running.
keys.copilotTokenPlaceholder: Copilot API token, or leave blank to use a GitHub App
keys.allowedModelsHelp: Select specific models this key applies to, or choose "Allow All Models" to allow all. Leave empty to deny all. Aliases must be added by their alias name - listing only the underlying model does not allow the alias (an alias best-model → gpt-4o requires "best-model" here, not just "gpt-4o").
keys.blockedModelsHelp: Models this key must never serve. The denylist always wins - if a model appears in both Allowed Models and here, it is blocked. Select "All Models" to block every model on this key. Aliases are matched by their alias name - blocking only the underlying model does not block aliases that point to it.
keys.deploymentsHelp: Map a request model name to the provider's identifier (deployment name, inference profile ID, etc.). Expand a row for canonical name, model family, and provider overrides - these drive cost logs and family-based routing.
keys.deploymentsHelpReplicate: Replicate deployments are listed only while "Use Deployments Endpoint" is on - otherwise type the owner/name and press Enter.
keys.azureDefaultHelp: Uses DefaultAzureCredential - automatically detects managed identity on Azure VMs and containers, workload identity in AKS, environment variables, and Azure CLI. No credentials required.
keys.azureScopesHelp: Optional OAuth scopes for token requests. By default we use https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default - add additional scopes here if your setup requires extra permissions.
keys.vertexAttachedHelp: Uses the service account attached to your environment (GCE, GKE, Cloud Run). No credentials required.
keys.projectNumberFineTuned: Project Number (Required only for fine-tuned models)
keys.vertexRegionHelp: Multi-region-only models are automatically routed to Google's matching multi-region endpoint. Turn on <medium>Force single region</medium> below to always use exactly this region.
keys.authCredentialsHelp: Service account JSON object or env.VAR_NAME
keys.credsStoredSecurely: Credentials are stored securely. Edit to update.
keys.apiKeyGeminiOnly: API Key (Supported only for gemini and fine-tuned models)
keys.forceSingleRegionHelp: Always call the region set above and skip automatic promotion of multi-region-only models to a multi-region endpoint. Enable when serving these models from a single region via provisioned throughput.
keys.useDeploymentsEndpointHelp: Sends every model on this key to /v1/deployments/{owner}/{name}/predictions, so plain model names stop working. To switch just one model, leave this off and set "Use deployments endpoint" on its row above.
keys.vllmUrlHelp: Base URL of the vLLM server (e.g. http://vllm-server:8000 or env.VLLM_URL)
keys.vllmModelHelp: Exact model name served on this vLLM instance
keys.databricksWorkspaceHelp: Your Databricks workspace URL (e.g. https://dbc-1234abcd-5678.cloud.databricks.com or env.DATABRICKS_WORKSPACE_URL)
keys.inferenceSurfaceHelp: Auto picks by model name: a dotted name such as system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5 goes to the Unity AI Gateway, anything else to Model Serving. Choose explicitly to pin one surface.
keys.patHelp: Generate one from Settings > Developer > Access tokens in your workspace.
keys.databricksClientIdPlaceholder: Service principal client ID or env.DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID
keys.forwardGovernanceTagsHelp: Sends the virtual key, team and customer names as Databricks-Ai-Gateway-Request-Tags, so Databricks usage tracking attributes spend the same way Bifrost does. Names only, never user identifiers.
keys.serverUrlHelp: Base URL of the {{server}} server (e.g. {{example}} or {{envVar}})
keys.copilotEither: Copilot accepts either credential. Fill in one of the two. GitHub App is the option for a shared gateway: usage bills to the organization that owns the installation and no individual Copilot seat is used. A Copilot API token in the field above is simpler but expires after about 30 minutes, so it suits testing rather than a running gateway. Set up a GitHub App for Copilot or get a Copilot API token.
keys.githubAppHelp: Leave these blank if you supplied a Copilot API token above. Otherwise all four are needed together. The App needs the Copilot Requests permission at Read & write, installed on the organization that should be billed with All repositories access, and that organization must allow Copilot requests from GitHub App installations.
keys.appIdHelp: The GitHub App's App ID or Client ID, from its settings page. <link>Create a GitHub App</link>
keys.installationIdHelp: The installation on the organization that should be billed. <link>Find your installation ID</link>
keys.repositoryIdHelp: Any repository the installation can access. Copilot's permission check requires one in the token request even though the installation itself needs All repositories access, so this is not really a scoping choice.
keys.privateKeyHelp: The App's private key in PEM form, as downloaded from GitHub. PKCS#1 and PKCS#8 both work.
keys.useAnthropicEndpointsHelp: Routes chat completions and responses requests through Anthropic-compatible endpoints.
keys.useOpenaiEndpointsHelp: Routes requests through Bedrock's OpenAI-compatible endpoints instead of Converse.
keys.iamRoleHelp: Uses IAM roles attached to your environment (EC2, Lambda, ECS, EKS).
keys.bearerApiKeyHelp: Uses a Bearer token for API key authentication.
keys.mantleApiKeyHelp: Uses a Bedrock Mantle API key sent as a Bearer token.
keys.mantleProjectIdHelp: Scopes Bedrock Mantle-routed models (OpenAI-family / Gemma) to a specific project via the OpenAI-Project header. Leave empty to use the account's default project.
keys.assumeRoleHelp: Assume an IAM role before requests. Works with both explicit credentials and inherited IAM (EC2, ECS, EKS).
keys.externalIdHelp: Required by the role's trust policy when using cross-account access
keys.externalIdHelpPeriod: Required by the role's trust policy when using cross-account access.
keys.batchRoleArnHelp: Service role Bedrock assumes for batch S3 access. When set, it takes priority over the role_arn sent in requests.
keys.mantleProjectHelp: Scopes inference and model listing to a specific Bedrock project (sent as the OpenAI-Project / anthropic-workspace-id header). Leave empty to use the account's default project.
keys.oauthM2mHelp: Databricks recommends OAuth machine-to-machine for production. Tokens are minted from the workspace OIDC endpoint and refreshed automatically.

virtualKeys.reassignTeamDescription: This key is currently assigned to another team. Reassigning it will move budget tracking to this team; future requests through this key will count against this team's budget, not the previous one.
virtualKeys.alignCalendarHelp: Reset budgets and rate limits at the start of each period (e.g. 1st of month) instead of rolling from creation date. Quarterly budgets always align to fiscal quarter starts. Applies to durations of a day or longer.
virtualKeys.resetUsageDescription: Enabling calendar alignment will reset budget usage to $0.00 and token/request rate-limit counters to 0 for this virtual key, then snap each reset date to the start of its current period (e.g. start of day, week, month, or year). The usage reset cannot be undone, but calendar alignment can be turned off later. This will take effect when you save.
virtualKeys.userAssignmentHelp: A virtual key can be assigned to only one user. If that user has an access profile, the key is adopted into it: it keeps working, but its providers, budgets, rate limits and MCP access are discarded and replaced by the profile's. This cannot be undone: a key inside a profile can be deleted, never released.
virtualKeys.rotateDescription: This will replace the secret value for "{{name}}". The key ID, budgets, rate limits, provider permissions, MCP access, and assignments stay the same. The previous key value stops working immediately unless a rotation cooldown is configured, in which case it remains valid until the cooldown ends.

routing.createDescription: Create a new CEL-based routing rule for intelligent request routing
routing.enableRuleHelp: Rule will be active and applied to matching requests
routing.chainRuleHelp: After this rule matches, re-evaluate routing rules using the resolved provider/model as the new context. Useful for composing rules, e.g. normalize a model alias first, then route based on the canonical name.
routing.priorityHelp: Lower numbers = higher priority (0 is highest)
routing.atLeastOneTarget: At least one routing target is required
routing.targetWeightGtZero: Each target weight must be greater than 0
routing.weightsMustSum: Target weights must sum to 1, current total: {{total}}
routing.ruleBuilderHelp: Build conditions to determine when this rule should apply. Leave empty to apply this rule to all requests.
routing.governanceNote: Note: Ensure token limits, request limits, and budget are configured in Model Providers → Configurations → {provider} → Governance (provider-level) or Model Providers → Budgets & Limits section (model-level) before using them in routing rules.
routing.routingTargetsHelp: Weights must sum to 1. Leave provider or model empty to use the incoming request value.
routing.fallbacksHelp: Provider is required, but model is optional. Leave model empty to use the incoming request value.
routing.fallbacksOrder: Fallbacks will be used in the order they are defined
routing.apiKeyOptional: API Key <muted>(optional; leave unset for load-balanced selection)</muted>
routing.definedAsCel: Defined as a CEL expression below
routing.chainRuleTooltip: After this rule matches, routing rules are re-evaluated using the resolved provider/model as the new context.
routing.mobileHelp: Use the routing rules list to review and modify rules on mobile.
routing.staticChainHelp: Re-entry point is fully proven by static analysis; every condition on the path evaluated to a known value.
routing.dynamicChainHelp: Re-entry point is a conditional; one or more conditions on the path are not fully evaluated at build time.
